stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude for Word Beta With AI-Powered Tracked Changes

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched Claude for Word in public beta, bringing AI-powered editing directly into Microsoft Word as a native sidebar add-in for Team and Enterprise users on Mac and Windows.
All AI-generated edits surface as Microsoft Word's tracked changes, enabling users to accept or reject each suggestion as they would a human collaborator's markup.
Claude for Word shares context across Anthropic's Office add-in family — a single conversation thread can span Word, Excel, and PowerPoint documents simultaneously.
The add-in can interpret existing Word comment threads and deliver revisions that directly address each note, returning an updated document with tracked changes.
The launch positions Anthropic in direct competition with Microsoft's own 365 Copilot, though early users noted Claude's smoother document-handling and more coherent multi-app context flow.

stories.headline: Anthropic Hires Microsoft AI Platform Lead Eric Boyd as Head of Infrastructure

key_facts.fact: Anthropic hired Eric Boyd from Microsoft to serve as Head of Infrastructure, overseeing the buildout of systems for its AI services.
At Microsoft, Boyd oversaw the company's AI platform and managed a team of approximately 1,500 employees.
Anthropic has committed to spending $50 billion to build AI data centers in the United States.
The hire comes as Anthropic faces increasing usage of its models, including Claude Code, and has experienced occasional service disruptions tied to heavy usage.

stories.headline: Bank of Canada and Bank of England Mobilize on AI Cyber Risks After Mythos

key_facts.fact: The Bank of Canada met with major financial firms on Friday (April 11) to discuss cybersecurity implications of Anthropic's Mythos model, and the Bank of England is preparing its own meeting with banking and insurance executives.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell had convened an emergency meeting earlier in the week with CEOs of Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo at Treasury headquarters.

The meetings were triggered by Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview, which the company says can identify and exploit vulnerabilities across every major operating system and browser, and autonomously discovered a 27-year-old flaw in OpenBSD.

Anthropic launched Mythos Preview on April 7 in deliberately limited capacity via Project Glasswing, with partners including AWS, Apple, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Cisco, CrowdStrike, JPMorganChase, and Palo Alto Networks.
Anthropic committed up to $100 million in Mythos usage credits to Project Glasswing partners. The model is priced at $25/$125 per million input/output tokens for participants.

Powell's participation signaled that AI-driven cyber threats are being treated as a systemic risk to the financial system, not a narrow industry concern, according to people familiar with the discussions.

stories.headline: Generalist AI Unveils GEN-1 Robotics Model Claiming 99% Success on Physical Tasks

key_facts.fact: Generalist AI introduced GEN-1, an embodied foundation model that achieves 99% success rates on certain physical tasks, up from 64% for GEN-0, while completing tasks up to 3x faster.
The company describes GEN-1 as 'the first general-purpose AI model that crosses a new performance threshold: mastery of simple physical tasks.'
GEN-1 requires roughly one hour of robot-specific data to adapt to new tasks, using large-scale pretraining on human activity data collected through wearable devices.
Demonstrations showed robots performing tasks such as folding boxes, packing items, and assembling components over extended periods with hundreds or thousands of repetitions and minimal errors.

stories.headline: Analysts Say Google's TurboQuant LLM Compression Will Expand, Not Reduce, Memory Demand

key_facts.fact: Google's TurboQuant compression algorithm, detailed in March, can reduce KV cache memory usage by 6x and boost inference speed by 8x for large language models.

Despite initial fears that sent memory stocks lower, analysts and researchers now say TurboQuant is more likely to expand memory chip demand than reduce it — by removing bottlenecks, it enables training of bigger, more capable models.
LLM parameter counts have grown from 0.09 billion in 2019 to over 1 trillion today; more efficient memory use historically drives demand for larger models rather than reducing total consumption.
FT analysis cites experts concluding that more efficient AI could mean even greater need for semiconductors, reinforcing the Jevons paradox in AI compute.
Memory industry context: DRAM contract prices surged 55-60% QoQ in Q1 2026, with HBM now consuming 23% of total DRAM wafer output, up from 19% the prior year.

stories.headline: Hungary Votes in Landmark Election That Could End Orbán's 16-Year Grip on Power

key_facts.fact: Hungary holds parliamentary elections on April 12 in what is seen as PM Viktor Orbán's biggest political test in 16 years of rule. Challenger Péter Magyar's Tisza party leads by double digits in most independent polls.
Magyar, 45, is a former member of Fidesz's inner circle and ex-husband of Orbán's justice minister. He burst into prominence in 2024 during a presidential pardon scandal.
Orbán has campaigned on external dangers including the Ukraine war and his close relationship with Trump. VP Vance made a two-day visit to Budapest earlier in the campaign.

The election is closely watched internationally. An Orbán defeat would impact the network of right-wing parties across Europe and the transatlantic relationship, given his ties to both Putin and Trump.
Magyar promises EU reengagement and unfreezing billions in EU funds withheld from Hungary, while his supporters chanted 'Európa! Európa!' at his final rally in Debrecen.

stories.headline: Japan Approves Additional $4B for Rapidus, Bringing Total Chip Subsidies to $14.8B

key_facts.fact: Japan's METI approved an additional ¥631.5 billion ($3.96 billion) in R&D support for chipmaker Rapidus on April 11.
Total government R&D support for Rapidus now amounts to ¥2.354 trillion (~$14.8 billion).
Rapidus targets mass production of 2-nanometre logic semiconductors in the latter half of fiscal year 2027.
NEDO also decided to support semiconductor design-related projects by Fujitsu and IBM Japan.
An opening ceremony was held for a newly built semiconductor analysis center and R&D base in Chitose City, Hokkaido, attended by METI Minister Ryosei Akazawa.
In February, Rapidus secured a combined investment of about ¥160 billion from private companies, with a planned ¥250 billion from the government.

stories.headline: Linux Kernel Publishes Official AI Coding Guidelines: Humans Must Own Every Line

key_facts.fact: The Linux kernel project published new documentation allowing AI-generated code contributions, provided they comply with existing kernel guidelines, licensing, and attribution requirements.

AI agents are explicitly banned from adding Signed-off-by tags. Only humans can legally certify the Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO), and the submitter takes full responsibility for all AI-generated code.
A new 'Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION' attribution tag is required when AI played a meaningful role, creating a disclosure mechanism to track AI-assisted contributions across the kernel.

Linus Torvalds said he doesn't want the documentation to become a 'political battlefield' over AI, noting 'zero point in talking about AI slop' since bad actors who submit garbage AI code won't disclose it anyway.
All AI-assisted code must comply with the kernel's existing GPL-2.0-only licensing, use appropriate SPDX license identifiers, and follow the same processes as human-written code.

stories.headline: OpenAI Accuses Musk of 'Legal Ambush' as $100B+ Trial Set for April 27

key_facts.fact: OpenAI filed a court response on April 11 describing Elon Musk's recent lawsuit amendments as a 'legal ambush' that is 'legally improper and factually unsupported.'
Musk shifted his stance to ask that any financial award be returned directly to OpenAI rather than to himself, after previously seeking $79–134 billion in personal damages.

Musk expanded his lawsuit to explicitly target Microsoft, alleging wrongful gains from OpenAI's shift toward a for-profit model, and proposed structural changes including leadership changes at OpenAI.
OpenAI argued the amendments introduce 'entirely new theories of liability' and prejudice OpenAI's ability to prepare a defense, requiring new proof and witnesses.
The trial between OpenAI and Musk is scheduled for April 27, with damages potentially exceeding $100 billion, making it one of the largest trials in US history.

stories.headline: OpenAI Discloses North Korean Supply Chain Attack via Compromised Axios Library

key_facts.fact: A GitHub Actions workflow used to sign OpenAI's macOS apps downloaded a malicious version of the Axios JavaScript library on March 31, during a ~3-hour window when the package was compromised.
The compromised workflow had access to certificate and notarisation material used to sign macOS applications including ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Codex-cli, and Atlas.
OpenAI said the signing certificate was likely not successfully extracted by the malicious payload and found no evidence that user data, systems, or IP were compromised.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group attributed the Axios npm package compromise to a suspected North Korean threat actor tracked as UNC1069, who hijacked a maintainer's account via AI-enabled social engineering.
Axios, one of npm's most widely used HTTP client libraries with ~100 million weekly downloads, was compromised for about three hours after attackers slipped a remote-access trojan into two releases.
OpenAI attributed the root cause to a misconfiguration in its GitHub Actions workflow, which has since been corrected. All macOS users are required to update to the latest app versions.

stories.headline: Chinese Nvidia Cloud Partner Procured 300 Servers With Banned AI GPUs Worth $92M

key_facts.fact: Invoice records from China's State Taxation Administration reveal Sharetronic Data Technology procured almost 300 servers containing banned Nvidia AI chips, worth $92 million.
Sharetronic sold 276 Super Micro SYS-821GE-TNHR and 32 Dell PowerEdge XE9680 servers to a Shenzhen subsidiary in May and June 2025, containing banned Nvidia H100 or H200 chips.
Both Super Micro and Dell denied selling products to Sharetronic or having it as a registered customer.
Sharetronic's shares hit the 20% daily drop limit after the arrest of Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw on smuggling charges.
Sharetronic claimed all assets came from 'legal and compliant channels' but declined to reveal the source of the servers.

stories.headline: SpaceX Launches Cygnus XL to ISS Carrying East Africa's First Climate Camera

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 carrying Northrop Grumman's Cygnus XL cargo ship to the ISS from Cape Canaveral at 7:41 a.m. EDT on April 11, delivering over 5,000 kg (11,000 lbs) of supplies and experiments.
The payload includes ClimCam, a joint Earth-observation camera from Kenya, Uganda, and Egypt — the first climate-focused instrument from East Africa to reach the ISS.
ClimCam uses multispectral imaging combined with AI to generate near-real-time climate and weather data, targeting floods, droughts, and extreme weather in East Africa.

The camera will be installed on the Airbus-operated Bartolomeo platform on the ISS Columbus module and operate for 6-12 months. The project was selected via a UN Office for Outer Space Affairs competition.
The Falcon 9 booster (B1094, 7th flight) landed successfully at Landing Zone 40. This was SpaceX's 652nd launch overall and 43rd of 2026.

organizations: UN Office for Outer Space Affairs

stories.headline: Ukraine and Russia Swap 175 POWs Each, Begin 32-Hour Orthodox Easter Ceasefire

key_facts.fact: Ukraine and Russia exchanged 175 prisoners of war each on April 11, with Ukraine also receiving 7 civilians from Russian captivity. Most Ukrainian servicemen had been held since 2022.
The United Arab Emirates mediated the exchange. Russia also returned 7 civilians originally from the Kursk region.
A 32-hour Easter ceasefire began at 4 p.m. local time (1300 GMT) on Saturday and was set to end at midnight on Sunday, as both countries celebrate Orthodox Easter.
163 of the freed Ukrainians had been held since 2022, marking over four years in captivity. Some had difficulty walking and were transported by ambulance.
US-brokered peace talks between Ukraine and Russia remain stalled over the issue of territory. POW exchanges are among the few concrete results from those negotiations.

stories.headline: Unitree H1 Humanoid Robot Hits 10 m/s Sprint, Nearing Usain Bolt's Peak Speed

key_facts.fact: On April 11, Unitree Robotics released footage of its H1 humanoid robot reaching a peak running speed of 10 meters per second (22.4 mph), setting a new world record for humanoid robots.
The H1 weighs approximately 62 kg with a leg length of 0.8 meters; the 10 m/s peak is a 200% increase over its previous record of 3.3 m/s set in early 2024.
Usain Bolt's 100m world record of 9.58 seconds translates to a peak speed of 12.42 m/s; the H1's 10 m/s is equivalent to a 10-second 100-meter dash.
Unitree CEO Wang Xingxing predicted in March at the Yabuli Forum that humanoids would outrun Bolt by mid-2026.
The H1 is far ahead of competitors: Tesla Optimus recently reached ~2.7 m/s (6 mph) and RobotEra STAR1 demonstrated 3.6 m/s (8 mph).

stories.headline: Unitree to Sell R1 Humanoid Robot Globally via AliExpress — First Marketplace Launch

key_facts.fact: Unitree Robotics will open sales of the R1 humanoid robot outside China via AliExpress next week, making it the first humanoid available for purchase on a general marketplace.
Sales will launch in North America, Europe, Japan, and Singapore; the R1 is 123 cm tall, weighs 27 kg, and sold in China from 29,900 yuan (~$4,100).
Unitree shipped over 5,500 R1 units in 2025 — more than Tesla, Figure AI, and Agility Robotics combined (each shipped approximately 150 units).
About 70% of R1 orders came from universities and research institutes; the company targets 10,000 to 20,000 units in 2026.
Over 80% of R1 components are manufactured in China, giving Unitree a significant cost advantage over Western competitors whose humanoids cost up to $300,000.

stories.headline: US Intel: China Preparing to Ship Air Defense Weapons to Iran via Third Countries

key_facts.fact: US intelligence indicates China is preparing to deliver shoulder-fired anti-air missile systems (MANPADs) to Iran within weeks, according to three people familiar with intelligence assessments.
Beijing is working to route shipments through third countries to mask their origin, two sources said. This would mark an escalation from dual-use technology to direct weapons transfers.
Trump warned China would face consequences: 'If China does that, China will have big problems, OK?' He is scheduled to visit Beijing next month for talks with Xi Jinping.
Chinese Embassy denied the claim: 'China has never provided weapons to any party to the conflict; the information in question is untrue.'

The intelligence suggests Iran may be using the ceasefire to replenish weapons with help from foreign partners. A US F-15 was shot down over Iran last week reportedly by a 'handheld shoulder missile.'

stories.headline: US-Iran Islamabad Peace Talks End Without Deal After 21 Hours Over Nuclear Impasse

key_facts.fact: US Vice President JD Vance announced the talks ended without agreement after 21 hours, saying Iran refused to commit to not developing nuclear weapons.
The talks were the first face-to-face engagement between the US and Iran since 2015, and the highest-level discussions since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

Iran demanded release of $6 billion in frozen assets, guarantees around its nuclear program, the right to charge ships through the Strait of Hormuz, and an end to Israeli strikes on Hezbollah in Lebanon.
Vance left a 'final and best offer' on the table, saying 'We'll see if the Iranians accept it,' leaving a narrow path for a future agreement.
The war has killed at least 3,000 people in Iran, 2,020 in Lebanon, 23 in Israel, and more than a dozen in Gulf Arab states since US-Israeli strikes began on Feb. 28.
Chinese, Egyptian, Saudi and Qatari officials were in Islamabad to indirectly facilitate the talks, reflecting the global stakes of the negotiations.

stories.headline: US Navy Transits Strait of Hormuz for First Time Since Iran War Began, Starts Mine Clearing

key_facts.fact: Two US Navy guided-missile destroyers passed through the Strait of Hormuz on April 11, the first American warship transit since the Iran war began six weeks ago.
Trump posted on Truth Social that the US has started clearing the strait and that 'all 28' of Iran's mine-dropping boats 'are lying at the bottom of the sea.'
Iranian state TV denied any US ships had crossed the strait. Iran's military command denied reports about the passage.
The strait's effective closure for ~40 days has disrupted global energy markets and sent oil and gasoline prices soaring, despite most oil flowing through it not going to the US.
Three Liberian- and Chinese-flagged supertankers also passed through the strait on Saturday, the first commercial vessels to exit the Gulf since the ceasefire last week.
